brief.headline: Cut price by 3% to match our best Dextrose supplier (Sayaji) and save ₹1.26 Cr a year

priceAsk.summary: Bring Dextrose down to ₹66.48/KG — the price Sayaji Industries already gives us
priceAsk.basis: We pay them ₹68.45/KG, which is 3.0% more than the ₹66.48/KG Sayaji charges us for the same material. The open market typically asks ₹66–73/kg, so ₹66.48/KG sits well within the fair band and is proven — we already buy at that price.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep 30 Days After Receipt — no change needed

brief.financialLeverage: Gujarat Ambuja publishes no financials, so we can't see their cash position or profit. But we know they get ₹21.21 Cr a year from us for Dextrose — 56% of our total Dextrose spend — so we're a big piece of their business. That size gives us room to ask, but because we rely on them for more than half our Dextrose we need to line up a qualified second source first. Push firmly on price, but don't corner them until we have that backup ready to go.

evidence.point: We pay them ₹1.26 Cr more per year than we need to
Their Dextrose price is 3% above our best price
Our best Dextrose price today is from Sayaji Industries
We spend heavily with them — more than a fifth of our procurement budget
They supply 56% of our Dextrose — we're concentrated
Open-market asking prices for Anhydrous Dextrose IP typically run ₹66–73/kg, so our target sits in the fair range

alternates.name: Tirupati Starch & Chemicals Ltd
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): listed Indore maize wet-miller that makes Dextrose ANHYDROUS at IV-fluid grade — an exact form match; ask for IP monograph CoA to confirm.

alternates.name: Gulshan Polyols Ltd
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): listed starch and polyol maker, established in dextrose and sorbitol — described as a drop-in alternate to Gujarat Ambuja and Sayaji.

alternates.name: Roquette India Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: A lead to qualify (verify before RFQ): Indian arm of a global starch major; makes pharma-grade dextrose and excipients; premium and very reliable (revenue ₹2898.05 Cr, health score D 28/100).

risks: They supply 56% of our Dextrose (₹21.21 Cr), so squeezing too hard before we have a second source approved could leave us scrambling if they walk or tighten allocation.
Their financials aren't public, so we're flying blind on whether they're cash-tight or stable — lean on our own purchase data and the market benchmark, not assumptions about their balance sheet.

The market asking price band is wide (₹60–81/kg) and our target ₹66.48/KG sits at the low end of the typical range (₹66–73/kg), so expect them to defend their current ₹68.45/KG as fair; counter with the fact we already pay less to Sayaji.
All three strongest alternates are leads from public research — none are qualified, audited or priced yet — so treat them as a pipeline to build, not a card to play today.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and we'd like to close the 3% gap between your Dextrose price and the ₹66.48/KG we already pay Sayaji — can we work toward that benchmark this year?
